rfi.title: World set to breach 1.5C climate limit as UN urges rapid reversal
rfi.description: Global warming is set to cross the 1.5C limit within the next few years, exposing people and ecosystems to more severe climate damage, the UN's environmental agency said on Wednesday. But temperatures could eventually be brought back down if emissions fall sharply and carbon dioxide is removed from the atmosphere.

rfi.title: French pop star Patrick Bruel cancels 35-date tour amid sexual assault storm
rfi.description: French pop and variety singer Patrick Bruel has cancelled his entire 35-date autumn tour, bowing to weeks of pressure from politicians, mayors and feminist groups following allegations of sexual assault and rape against him. Lawyers representing the accusers called the decision a "power signal" showing that women are "at last being heard."

rfi.title: Senegal and IMF strike $2.2bn deal, two years after debt scandal froze funding
rfi.description: Senegal and the International Monetary Fund have reached a staff-level agreement on a new $2.2 billion (€1.9 billion) lending programme, nearly two years after an earlier deal was suspended following the discovery of previously unreported public debt.

rfi.title: Macron opens Bayeux Tapestry exhibition before first Burnham talks
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron begins a two-day visit to Britain on Wednesday, opening a landmark exhibition of the Bayeux Tapestry, the 11th-century embroidery depicting the Norman conquest of England, before holding his first in-depth talks with new Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Thursday.

rfi.title: France-UK deal linked to seven-year low in Channel migrant crossings
rfi.description: France and the UK saw the number of small boats carrying migrants across the English Channel fall to its lowest summer level since 2019, with London crediting a new enforcement deal between the two countries.

rfi.title: Nepal glacier disaster toll passes 1,000 as calls for climate justice grow
rfi.description: The death toll from last week's devastating Himalayan glacial floods passed 1,000 on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors. Nepal's foreign minister said the disaster was "a warning signal" of the growing risks posed by climate change.

rfi.title: DRC school year begins amid Ebola, strikes and conflict
rfi.description: Millions of students returned to school across the Democratic Republic of Congo on Tuesday, but the new term began amid an Ebola outbreak affecting six provinces, a teachers’ strike call and continuing conflict in the east. In AFC/M23-controlled territories, the movement organised the return to classrooms even as Kinshasa continued to pay primary and secondary school teachers.

rfi.title: French clubs cash in as Ligue 1 transfer window comes to a close
rfi.description: The transfer window for French football clubs closed on Tuesday evening after three months of trading that saw the 18 Ligue 1 sides splash out €522 million and reap €894 million in player sales.

rfi.title: French schools start new year in shadow of summer cyberattack
rfi.description: Millions of pupils are returning to classrooms across France on Tuesday for the start of the new school year, with some schools forced to fall back on paper timetables and registers after a major cyberattack disrupted education systems over the summer.

rfi.title: Russia’s return to G20 talks unsettles Europe as Iran and trade tensions loom
rfi.description: Russia's presence at the opening of G20 meetings in North Carolina sparked pushback from Europe on Monday, adding fresh tension to talks already clouded by the Iran war and US President Donald Trump's trade policies.

rfi.title: Ukraine air defences top agenda as EU ministers meet in Ireland
rfi.description: European Union defence and foreign ministers gathering in Ireland this week are set to focus on strengthening Ukraine’s air defences, as concern grows over both Russia’s intensifying bombardment and what European officials see as a widening campaign of destabilisation across the continent.

rfi.title: France takes aim at fast-fashion giants with new pricing penalties
rfi.description: France will start imposing fees on ultra-fast fashion from Tuesday, with charges set to rise to almost €20 per garment as the government steps up pressure on major Asian e-commerce platforms including Shein.

rfi.title: From labels to Netflix, how Quebec's fight to protect French collides with US trade
rfi.description: French-language protections in Quebec have emerged as an unlikely source of friction between Canada and the United States, bringing rules designed to protect French in overwhelmingly English-speaking North America into a much bigger fight over trade.

rfi.title: No more Messi nights for Argentina as skipper says adios to national squad
rfi.description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino led the tributes to Argentina skipper Lionel Messi, who announced his retirement from international football just over a month after playing in the 2026 World Cup final.

rfi.title: 'Devoted servant of the nation': Former French PM Édouard Balladur dies aged 97
rfi.description: Former French prime minister Édouard Balladur died in Paris late Monday at the age of 97, his family said. Born in Turkey, he served as former president Francois Mitterrand's last prime minister from March 1993 to May 1995, carrying out several major privatisations of state companies, and unsuccessfully ran for the top job in 1995.

rfi.title: Ten years after Gabon’s post-election violence, painful questions remain
rfi.description: Ten years on, victims of violence that followed president Ali Bongo’s disputed re-election in Gabon are still demanding truth and justice. Questions also remain over the possible involvement of French nationals and the response of the French authorities.

rfi.title: Niger coup attempt: 'Russians saved the day' analyst tells RFI
rfi.description: Niger’s military government has survived its most serious internal challenge since seizing power in 2023, after Russian paramilitaries helped loyalist forces crush last Saturday's attempted coup in the capital, Niamey. RFI spoke to an expert who explains how this episode has left General Abdourahamane Tiani’s junta weakened and more dependent on Russia.

rfi.title: French high schools scramble to work out rules as phone ban takes effect
rfi.description: The new school year starts on Tuesday in France, and with it comes a new rule: mobile phones will no longer be allowed in high schools. The ban came into force a week before the first day of term, leaving schools with little time to work out how to put it into practice.

bbc.description: Russia is accused of growing increasingly reckless after Berlin blamed Russia for a failed drone attack on Leipzig airport.

bbc.title: Nepal intensifies relief and recovery efforts after deadly floods, UN says
bbc.description: More than 1,000 people have died and thousands are missing, as rescue efforts continue and aid is airlifted to villages.

bbc.title: Lizzo 'grateful' after judge dismisses lawsuit against production company
bbc.description: The About Damn Time singer says she is "relieved" at the outcome and will "continue to fight" every claim.

bbc.title: BBC travels inside occupied Lebanon as officials say Israel expanding positions
bbc.description: A BBC team joined a humanitarian mission of the UN peacekeeping force, which says Israeli troops are fortifying positions and continuing demolitions.

bbc.title: Bus crash on Egypt's Red Sea coast kills 22

bbc.title: South Korea jails care home head for sexually assaulting disabled residents
bbc.description: The man, surnamed Kim, was handed a 15-year prison term for abusing three residents at the facility near Seoul.

bbc.title: Tiger Woods changes plea, gets five-year driving ban
bbc.description: The golfer will accept a five-year driving ban and $1,000 fine as part of a plea agreement.

bbc.title: Ariana Grande makes emotional tour exit and steps back from public life
bbc.description: The star makes an emotional farewell as she wraps up a tour she's described as her "last hurrah".

bbc.title: Remarkable US oil deal puzzles analysts - and angers many Venezuelans
bbc.description: Amounting to 65 billion barrels of crude, the deal is labelled by one ex-envoy as a colonialist "fever dream".

bbc.title: Could the man who murdered a Christian missionary and his sons walk free in India?
bbc.description: Dara Singh is serving a life sentence for burning alive Graham Staines and his two sons in Odisha in 1999.

bbc.title: Will self-flying planes transform the skies?
bbc.description: Autonomous crop-spraying aircraft are leading the way in pilot-free flying.

bbc.description: As of August, the number forced to return this year from Pakistan and Iran had reached another million.

euronews.title: How horse milk ‘kymyz’ became a drink still in demand thousands of years later
euronews.description: Fermented horse milk, known as kymyz, is a traditional Central Asian drink with thousands of years of history. In Kazakhstan, it remains an important part of nomadic heritage, cuisine and hospitality.

euronews.title: Iranian rial in freefall as dollar breaks 2.1 million mark
euronews.description: The rial has lost 63% of its value against the dollar since March, with the euro hitting 2.55 million rials and gold coins changing hands at 2.26 billion. Iran's central bank governor pledged a $2 billion injection while acknowledging inflation had placed "heavy pressure on people's livelihoods."

euronews.description: The transfer was carried out partially by buying and selling and partly by physically transferring gold, the Dutch national bank said.

euronews.title: Von der Leyen: Russian drone incidents in Europe are the 'new normal'
euronews.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Europe must prepare for a “new era of European security” after Russia was blamed for a drone sabotage incident last month. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said the Alliance must have the capabilities it needs to address such threats.

euronews.title: Brussels will not mediate between US and Canada, EU trade chief says
euronews.description: Maroš Šefčovič said the Commission is ready to explore a wide range of options to deepen cooperation with Ottawa as Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney calls for a closer partnership with the EU.

euronews.title: From infrastructure to military drills, China deepens footprint in Egypt as Xi visits Cairo
euronews.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping’s return to Cairo comes as Egypt and China push their relationship beyond infrastructure and trade into technology, defence and a broader strategic partnership with regional implications.

euronews.title: 'An issue that concerns the entire EU': Italy's FM warns of possible Russian meddling in general election
euronews.description: Surveys show that the cost of living, a deteriorating public health system, security and immigration are among Italians' top concerns when they head to the polls.

euronews.title: Spain calls for probe into reports government agency blamed Morocco for Ceuta migrant influx
euronews.description: Although the vast majority of the around 70,000 migrants returned to Morocco within hours, thousands remain in Ceuta with many living rough on the streets.

euronews.description: The EU is preparing new sanctions on 27 Russian individuals and entities involved in the deportation and indoctrination of Ukrainian children, ahead of a September conference in Toronto on their return.

euronews.title: The World’s 50 Best Hotels 2026: 16 hotels in Europe feature on extended 50-100 list
euronews.description: Ahead of The World’s 50 Best Hotels 2026 unveiling on 15 September, an extended ranking sees 16 properties in Europe included in the 50-100 list.

euronews.title: Europe vows to stay united as hybrid war activity surges
euronews.description: Europe and Canada have said they won't succumb to the growing number of hybrid attacks from Russia. The show of unity comes as Germany takes the unprecedented step of formally blaming to the Kremlin for a drone incident at Leipzig airport last month.

euronews.title: Kyiv school year begins under the shadow of air raid sirens
euronews.description: Kyiv children began the new school year with a ceremony interrupted by an air raid alert, hours after Russian missile strikes hit the capital.

lemonde.title: Nicholas Cullinan, directeur du British Museum : « Tout le monde a conscience que le prêt de la tapisserie de Bayeux est extraordinaire »
lemonde.description: A huit jours de l’ouverture de l’exposition au public, inaugurée mercredi 2 septembre par Emmanuel Macron et le roi Charles III, le directeur du musée londonien revient sur la folle aventure qu’ont constituée le prêt et le transfert de la France à l’Angleterre de cette œuvre monumentale.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Kiev prévient les instances internationales que « l’espace aérien russe n’est pas sûr »
lemonde.description: « Sur fond d’escalade drastique de la terreur exercée par la Russie contre l’Ukraine, l’espace aérien russe devient de plus en plus dangereux », a déclaré le chef de la diplomatie ukrainienne, Andrii Sybiha, citant « l’augmentation de l’activité militaire » et appelant « chacun à l’éviter ».

lemonde.title: « La trajectoire d’Edouard Balladur offre un certain nombre de leçons aux prétendants d’aujourd’hui »
lemonde.description: La disparition de l’ancien premier ministre de cohabitation de François Mitterand, défait par Jacques Chirac en 1995, est riche d’enseignements à l’aube d’une nouvelle campagne présidentielle, estime dans sa chronique Solenn de Royer, journaliste au « Monde ».

lemonde.title: Radio France : les personnels demandent le retrait de la chronique de Charles Sapin sur France Inter et votent la grève
lemonde.description: Dans une motion adoptée à l’unanimité, les personnels expriment leur « refus catégorique » de l’arrivée de Charles Sapin à l’antenne, dont le magazine porte des valeurs non « compatibles » avec celles du groupe public.

lemonde.title: Après la tentative de coup d’Etat au Niger, Alger inaugure sa nouvelle doctrine de déploiement militaire hors de ses frontières
lemonde.description: Afin de préserver ses intérêts stratégiques au Sahel, Alger a dépêché à Niamey une formation aérienne composée de Soukhoï et d’Iliouchine au lendemain d’une tentative de putsch. L’initiative marque une rupture dans la tradition algérienne de non-intervention militaire à l’étranger.

lemonde.title: « J’ai su profiter des taux faibles, je gagne de l’argent dans cette affaire » : le T3 d’Alexandre, jeune banquier, à Valenciennes
lemonde.description: « Et toi, t’habites où ? » En pleine crise du logement, étudiants et jeunes actifs redéfinissent, souvent malgré eux, l’art de trouver un chez-soi. Cette semaine, Alexandre, 30 ans, a acheté son logement dans le Nord et en a fait un lieu à son image.

lemonde.title: Les Pays-Bas transfèrent 86 tonnes d’or des Etats-Unis et du Canada vers le Royaume-Uni, invoquant « l’instabilité géopolitique croissante »
lemonde.description: Le mouvement a été réalisé en partie par des opérations d’achat et de vente, et par transport physique. Concrètement, plus de 27 tonnes d’or physique ont été transférées des Etats-Unis et du Canada vers les Pays-Bas avant de gagner Londres.

lemonde.title: Un projet gouvernemental sur les droits à la retraite pour les parents d’au moins trois enfants sème l’inquiétude
lemonde.description: Plusieurs associations familiales et syndicats s’interrogent après l’annonce faite, mardi, par le ministre du travail, Jean-Pierre Farandou, d’une possible refonte des règles sur les majorations de pension pour les personnes ayant eu au moins trois enfants, afin d’« égaliser les droits familiaux entre les femmes et les hommes ».

lemonde.title: La « bataille des gauches », un feuilleton centenaire : retour sur des dissensions aussi anciennes que le mouvement socialiste
lemonde.description: Si l’histoire de la gauche est ponctuée de scissions sur des questions stratégiques ou des conflits de valeurs, la culture de la division semble s’exacerber aujourd’hui, à mesure que son poids politique s’affaiblit. Avant une nouvelle union ?

lemonde.title: Au Venezuela, Chevron obtient de nouveaux gisements de pétrole alors que le ministre de l’énergie américain est en visite dans le pays
lemonde.description: Cette annonce a lieu quelques jours après celle d’un accord pétrolier entre les Etats-Unis et le Venezuela, approuvé mardi par l’Assemblée nationale et l’armée vénézuéliennes.

lemonde.title: Fibre Excellence : la région Occitanie appelle l’Etat à la rescousse et demande une nationalisation temporaire du papetier
lemonde.description: Placée en redressement judiciaire, l’entreprise de Haute-Garonne, leader français de la fabrication de pâte à papier, a 90 millions d’euros à trouver avant le 8 septembre. La présidente de région, Carole Delga, demande à l’Etat de rentrer temporairement au capital.

lemonde.title: Le réseau électrique européen face aux menaces de sabotage et de cyberattaques : « Le scénario du pire n’a rien d’inéluctable, mais il faut s’y préparer »
lemonde.description: Dans un contexte de conflictualité croissante avec la Russie, le risque d’un black-out majeur en Europe est pris au sérieux. La France veut organiser un exercice de simulation de crise en 2027.

lemonde.title: Une idée « interdite par les traités européens » : le président de la Bundesbank s’oppose à l’annulation de la dette proposée par Jean-Luc Mélenchon
lemonde.description: Joachim Nagel critique fermement la proposition du candidat « insoumis » à la présidentielle d’annuler les 18 % de dette de la France possédée par la Banque centrale européenne.

lemonde.title: « Gouffres et merveilles » : deux amis embarqués dans un road-movie introspectif
lemonde.description: Le réalisateur Jean Boiron Lajous et l’ingénieure du son Christine Dancausse confrontent leurs traumatismes familiaux lors d’un trajet en voiture plein d’imprévus.

lemonde.title: L’Iran réplique aux attaques américaines en visant des bases états-uniennes dans plusieurs pays du Golfe
lemonde.description: Téhéran a attaqué mercredi des bases américaines aux Emirats arabes unis, au Koweït et à Bahreïn, après la conclusion d’une deuxième salve de frappes lancées par les Etats-Unis. Quelques heures auparavant, le président iranien, Massoud Pezeshkian, avait plaidé pour une reprise des négociations.

lemonde.title: En Norvège, Mette-Marit, une reine fragilisée
lemonde.description: Greffée des deux poumons en juin, la nouvelle reine de Norvège est montée sur le trône aux côtés de son époux, Haakon VIII, pendant sa convalescence. Malgré l’empathie que suscite sa situation, les nombreux scandales qui se sont succédé autour d’elle en font une personnalité très controversée dans le royaume.

france24fr.title: En Allemagne, deux postes électriques visés par des actes de sabotage en 24 heures
france24fr.description: De nouveaux actes de sabotage ont eu lieu mardi en Allemagne, visant des postes électriques. Les enquêteurs soupçonnent "un sabotage téléguidé par un État étranger" ou un acte "d'extrémiste de gauche".

france24fr.title: Sud-Liban : les difficiles missions de la Finul, prise en étau entre Israël et le Hezbollah
france24fr.description: Environ 6 % de la superficie du sud du Liban est occupée par l’armée israélienne depuis le printemps. Sur place, environ 600 soldats français de la Force intérimaire des Nations unies au Liban (Finul) y patrouillent encore. Cette mission de maintien de la paix de l'ONU constate et documente quotidiennement les violations du droit international de la part d'Israël et du Hezbollah, alors que son avenir s'écrit en pointillés. Un reportage de nos confrères de France 2.

france24fr.title: Burkina Faso : culture de l'ananas, un fruit tropical dans le Sahel
france24fr.description: 🇧🇫 Au Burkina Faso, des producteurs réussissent à cultiver l’ananas malgré un sol rouge, sableux et caillouteux, loin des terres tropicales auxquelles ce fruit est habituellement associé. Une adaptation qui repose sur l’innovation. 🍍

france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine : Kiev et Moscou intensifient leurs frappes
france24fr.description: Le président ukrainien a prévenu mardi l'aviation civile et les partenaires de Kiev que les drones ukrainiens rendraient dangereux d'emprunter l'espace aérien russe, un avertissement que son homologue russe a qualifié de "terroriste". Les précisions du général Dominique Trinquand, ancien chef de la mission militaire française auprès de l'ONU.

france24fr.title: Crues au Népal : l’ADN, dernier recours pour identifier les victimes
france24fr.description: Au Népal, après les crues dévastatrices, les familles continuent d’attendre des nouvelles de leurs proches disparus. Pour les corps retrouvés, souvent difficiles à identifier, les autorités exigent désormais une confirmation par ADN avant toute restitution. Les prélèvements se poursuivent, mais les résultats arrivent au compte-goutte.

france24fr.title: Drone de Leipzig : Vladimir Poutine dénonce les sanctions allemandes
france24fr.description: Les mesures des autorités allemandes contre la Russie annoncées mardi après que Berlin a formellement accusé Moscou d'avoir envoyé un drone chargé d'explosifs début août à l'aéroport de Leipzig sont "une nouvelle erreur", a affirmé le président russe Vladimir Poutine.

france24fr.title: Venezuela : l'Assemblée approuve l'accord pétrolier avec les Éats-Unis
france24fr.description: L'Assemblée nationale du Venezuela, où le pouvoir a la majorité absolue, a approuvé mardi l'accord "historique" sur le pétrole avec les Etats-Unis, qui contrôleront 17 gisements, accord qualifié d'opaque au sein de la société civile.

france24fr.title: Crue dans l'Himalaya : la Chine accusée de minimiser le bilan
france24fr.description: Des Tibétains en exil et des groupes de défense de la cause tibétaine accusent la Chine de largement sous-estimer le bilan des inondations dévastatrices dans les régions frontalières avec le Népal, ce que Pékin a rejeté comme une "campagne malveillante de dénigrement".

france24fr.title: Macron attendu à Londres pour l'inauguration de la tapisserie de Bayeux
france24fr.description: Le couple présidentiel français est reçu aujourd'hui à Londres pour l'inauguration de la broderie millénaire au British Museum. Un prêt volontaire du chef d'État, fait pour renforcer les relations franco-britanniques

france24fr.title: La Terre, une sphère difforme selon la Nasa ? Une confusion autour d'une représentation du globe
france24fr.description: Mi-juillet, la Nasa a publié sur son site une visualisation de la Terre sous la forme d'un "géoïde", modèle mathématique qui représente le champ gravitationnel de la Terre et considéré comme la forme la plus proche de la Terre. Mais une de ces visualisations, volontairement exagérée pour faire ressortir les zones affectées par la gravité, n'est pas à l'échelle, comme a dû le préciser la Nasa.

france24fr.title: Au Népal, l’insoutenable attente des proches de disparus
france24fr.description: Au Népal, l’espoir de retrouver des survivants s’amenuise de jour en jour. Dans les morgues, les corps s’accumulent et les capacités de stockage arrivent à saturation. Pour les proches des disparus, l’attente est insupportable. Ils passent d’un hôpital à l’autre, consultent les listes des rescapés et scrutent les photos des corps non identifiés. Les envoyés spéciaux de France 24 ont rencontré plusieurs de ces familles à la morgue de l’hôpital universitaire de Katmandou.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : un accord conclut avec le FMI pour relancer l’économie
france24fr.description: Le Sénégal et le FMI sont tombés d'accord pour la mise en place d'un programme d'aide de 2,2 milliards de dollars sur la période de 2026 - 2029. Cet accord doit encore être soumis à l'approbation du Conseil d'administration du Fonds monétaire international.

france24fr.title: "C'est dur" : au Sénégal, le ras-le-bol des ménages face à la vie chère
france24fr.description: Au Sénégal, la hausse des prix alimente la colère des ménages. Une campagne citoyenne réclame des mesures contre la vie chère, alors que Dakar a conclu mardi un accord de principe avec le FMI pour un programme d'aide de 2,2 milliards de dollars sur la période 2026-2029.

france24fr.title: Mercato : la Premier League casse la tirelire, la Ligue 1 ne sort pas le chéquier
france24fr.description: De l’Angleterre à l’Italie, en passant par l’Espagne et l’Allemagne, les grands clubs européens n’ont pas lésiné sur les dépenses cet été. En revanche, en France, la Ligue 1 a été plus timorée, réalisant plus de ventes que d'achats.

france24fr.title: Frappes américaines contre l'Iran : Téhéran mène une vaste riposte dans la région
france24fr.description: L'Iran a mené mercredi une riposte d'envergure au Moyen-Orient après une nouvelle salve de frappes sur son sol, qui ont notamment endeuillé un mariage dans le sud du pays selon Téhéran.

france24fr.title: Venezuela : le jackpot pétrolier de Donald Trump
france24fr.description: Le secrétaire américain à l’Énergie, Chris Wright, est à Caracas pour concrétiser un accord pétrolier hors norme. Pendant cent ans, une entreprise soutenue par Washington pourra exploiter 17 champs contenant près d’un cinquième des réserves vénézuéliennes.

france24fr.title: La tapisserie de Bayeux au British Museum : une exposition-évènement au coût exceptionnel
france24fr.description: L'exposition au British Museum de la tapisserie de Bayeux, qu'Emmanuel Macron visitera en avant-première mercredi, s'annonce comme l'événement de tous les superlatifs pour le musée londonien.

france24fr.title: Zelensky menace de perturber l’espace aérien russe avec des drones
france24fr.description: Le président ukrainien a prévenu lundi 1er septembre l'aviation civile et les partenaires de Kiev que les drones ukrainiens rendraient dangereux d'emprunter l'espace aérien russe, un avertissement que son homologue russe a qualifié de "terroriste".

nzz.title: Vom Hoffnungsträger zum Problemfall: Nestlé verkauft Vitaminmarken mit Milliardenverlust
nzz.description: Einst verfolgte Nestlé hochfliegende Pläne im Gesundheitsgeschäft. Der Konzernchef Philipp Navratil dampft sie ein.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Novartis baut in Basel bis zu 130 Stellen ab +++ Freihandelsabkommen Schweiz-Kosovo tritt im Oktober in Kraft
LIVE-TICKER - Amoktat in Aarau: Beschuldigter war psychisch krank und stellte sich am nächsten Tag selbst
nzz.description: Der festgenommene 43-jährige Schweizer sei «mit an Sicherheit grenzender Wahrscheinlichkeit» der Täter, sagt die Polizei. Der Mann hat in der Nacht auf Sonntag an einer Technoparty über 40 Mal in die Menge geschossen, eine 22-jährige Frau getötet und fünf weitere Personen verletzt.

nzz.title: Kurz vor der Präsidentschaftswahl holt ein Skandal Brasiliens Justizelite ein
nzz.description: Neue Ermittlungsakten belasten mächtige Richter des Landes und den Generalstaatsanwalt. Teile des Justizapparats versuchen nun die Ermittlungen gegen die eigenen Reihen zu stoppen.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Schweiz: Laurent Favre wird neues Verwaltungsratsmitglied der SRG
AfD erreicht höchsten je gemessenen Wert in einem Bundesland – alle Umfragen zur Wahl in Sachsen-Anhalt
nzz.description: Wie schneiden die Parteien vor der Wahl am 6. September in Umfragen ab, welche Koalitionen sind möglich – und was treibt die Menschen in Sachsen-Anhalt um? Hier gibt es die aktuellen Zahlen.

nzz.title: Die Netanyahus machen den 7. Oktober zur Familienangelegenheit
nzz.description: Sara Netanyahu unterstellt dem Oppositionspolitiker Yair Golan, er habe vom Hamas-Angriff vorab gewusst. Politische Konkurrenten sprechen von «kranken Verschwörungstheorien» – und wittern eine gezielte Kampagne.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Sturzflut von Nepal: Zahl der Todesopfer steigt auf über 1000 +++ Noch immer 600 Arbeiter von Wasserkraftwerken vermisst
nzz.description: Innerhalb weniger Minuten rissen Wasser, Geröll und Eis alles in der Grenzregion zwischen China und Nepal mit sich. Mehr als 1000 Personen kamen ums Leben, rund 4600 werden noch vermisst. Die wichtigsten Antworten zur Katastrophe im Himalaja-Tal.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Deutschland protestiert, und der russische Finanzminister parliert in den USA: So funktionieren Sanktionen nicht
nzz.description: Deutschland will Russland stärker zur Verantwortung ziehen – und Donald Trumps Regierung spricht in den USA mit dem russischen Finanzminister über Zusammenarbeit im internationalen Finanzsystem. Wenn Sanktionen wirken sollen, müssen sie gezielter und konsequenter eingesetzt werden.

nzz.title: «Tanker für Tanker»: Trump zündet in der Strasse von Hormuz die nächste Eskalationsstufe
nzz.description: Der Kampf um die Meerenge intensiviert sich erneut. Zum ersten Mal griffen die USA auch iranische Erdöltanker an. Teheran nahm im Gegenzug amerikanische Militärstützpunkte im Nahen Osten ins Visier. Trump ruft die Iraner erneut zum Umsturz auf.

nzz.title: Deutsch-russische Beziehungen am Tiefpunkt: Putin spricht nach deutschen Sanktionen von einem «schweren Fehler»
nzz.description: Der Kreml streitet eine Schuld am Drohnenvorfall in Leipzig kategorisch ab und stellt die deutschen Vorwürfe als Akt der Verzweiflung einer schwachen Regierung dar. Moskau hat bereits Gegenmassnahmen angekündigt.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Zwei Öltanker fahren in Strasse von Hormuz auf Seeminen +++ USA beenden Angriffswelle gegen Ziele in Iran
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Explosion am Bahnhof Augsburg – zwei Verletzte, Sperrung aufgehoben
nzz.description: Am frühen Morgen kam es am Bahnhof Augsburg zu einer Explosion. Die Polizei ist mit einem Grosseinsatz vor Ort. Der Zugverkehr wurde zeitweise eingestellt.

nzz.title: «Totalzusammenbruch» von Belinda Bencic: Gefrustet schlägt sie einen Ball ins Publikum, dann scheidet sie aus
nzz.description: Bencic entgeht einer Disqualifikation, unterliegt aber dennoch Julia Putinzewa am US Open in der ersten Runde. Mit ihr scheidet auch die letzte Schweizer Vertretung im Hauptfeld aus.

nzz.title: Rente oder Kapital aus der Pensionskasse: Bei vielen Banken, Versicherungen und Experten drohen Interessenkonflikte und Fehlberatungen
nzz.description: Immer mehr Pensionierte entscheiden sich beim Bezug des Pensionskassenvermögens für eine Auszahlung anstatt für die Rente. Dieser Entscheid hat Risiken. Der Pensionskassenverband reagiert.

observador.title: Registadas 23 agressões sexuais contra migrantes em Ceuta
observador.description: Ministério Público espanhol já identificou quatro marroquinos e três espanhóis responsáveis por agressões sexuais contra migrantes, algumas adolescentes, no enclave, durante o último mês.

observador.title: Jornalistas em greve ameaçam boicotar tomada de posse de PR
observador.description: Em causa está o incumprimento de memorandos assinados com o Governo, por falta de pagamento de subsídios e melhoria de condições de trabalho. Sindicato pede resolução "o mais rápido possível".

observador.title: Imigração ilegal. Mais de dois mil detidos em Nova Iorque
observador.description: Operação prendeu mais de dois mil imigrantes num mês. Casa Branca diz que autoridades estaduais se recusaram a colaborar. Presidente da Câmara de Nova acusa o ICE de aterrorizar imigrantes.

observador.title: Alga alastra na costa de Sines e ameaça biodiversidade local
observador.description: A presença desta espécie, de nome Rugulopteryx okamurae e com origem no mar Mediterrâneo, tem crescido bastante. Aumento da temperatura da água e anormal agitação marítima entre as principais causas.

observador.title: Petição para alterar carreira de técnico de diagnóstico
observador.description: Iniciativa pretende alterar o acordo de princípio alcançado entre Ministério e sindicatos sobre a nova carreira dos técnicos. Pede que revisão de carreira "não seja feita à custa do mérito adquirido".

observador.title: PSP recolhe 265 armas e seis mil munições em dois meses
observador.description: Ao longo de dois meses, foram feitas 140 ações de policiamento de proximidade, com o objetivo de "aproximar os serviços de armas e explosivos da PSP dos cidadãos".

observador.title: As notícias das 14h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Apoiante de Trump passa a crítico após deportação pelo ICE
observador.description: Milo Yiannopoulos, figura da 'alt-right' que apoiou Trump, foi detido em Nova Orleães e deportado. Agora diz sentir-se "muito envergonhado" por ter defendido política de imigração de Trump.

observador.title: Empresas de refeições escolares têm de faturar IVA de 13%
observador.description: Para a Autoridade Tributária, o serviço realizado "por entidades ou empresas fornecedoras de refeições a estabelecimentos de ensino ou a municípios não pode beneficiar" de isenção.

observador.title: Morreu o ator brasileiro Gracindo Júnior aos 83 anos
observador.description: Com uma carreira com mais de 50 anos, Gracindo Júnior destacou-se no teatro, no cinema e na televisão, tendo participado em várias produções de sucesso, incluindo "Rainha da Sucata".

observador.title: Espanha acusa governos europeus de amplificar desinformação
observador.description: Ministro dos Negócios Estrangeiros espanhol considerou inaceitável que os governos europeus "tenham contribuído para amplificar a desinformação" sobre a crise migratória em Ceuta.

observador.title: Luís Neves aguenta-se ou cai?
observador.description: No "Realpolitik", Sérgio Sousa Pinto e Miguel Pinheiro falam sobre o futuro do ministro da Administração Interna e sobre a guerra híbrida entre a Europa e a Rússia de Putin.

observador.title: Mercado medieval começa sexta-feira em Valença
observador.description: O mercado medieval vai contar com artesanato, artes e ofícios, danças, música, teatro, gastronomia, espetáculos de fogo e torneios apeados e a cavalo.

observador.title: 13h. Comissão Europeia condena ataques russos a Leipzig
observador.description: Ursula Von der Leyen diz estar solidária com o povo alemão. Ainda, Portugal vai convocar ainda hoje o embaixador da Rússia para discutir os ataques híbridos à Alemanha.

observador.title: Turistas encontram arma que pode resolver crime antigo
observador.description: Arma encontrada corresponde à pistola semiautomática suíça utilizada para matar três membros de uma família britânico-iraquiana e um ciclista francês. Procuradora diz que análise de arma é prioridade.

observador.title: Chega realça poucas condições da Alfândega de Ponta Delgada
observador.description: "São várias as denúncias públicas sobre a degradação do edifício da Alfândega de Ponta Delgada", afirma a deputada da Assembleia da República Ana Martins.

observador.title: ZERO defende "chumbo" de mina do Gavião, em Aljustrel
observador.description: Ambientalistas consideram que projeto da concessionária da mina de Aljustrel "ignora a ferrovia e exporta o minério sem uma estratégia de transformação", apelidando-o de "colónia mineira".

observador.title: Oliveira de Azeméis. Quase todos os concursos desertos
observador.description: Município lançou dois concursos públicos num total de 2,6 milhões de euros e, das sete obras neles propostas, só recebeu candidatura a uma empreitada de 559.568 euros.

zeit.title: Erntebericht 2026: Landwirtschaftsminister Rainer ruft »Krise nationaler Tragweite« aus
zeit.description: Wegen anhaltender Dürre ernteten Raps- und Getreidebauern in diesem Sommer rund zehn Prozent weniger. Agrarminister Alois Rainer kündigt weitere Finanzhilfen an.

zeit.title: Diebstahl in MV: Pflanzenschutzmittel im Wert von 90.000 Euro gestohlen
«Freedag is Plattdag»: Olaf Lies verrät seinen zweiten Lieblingsspruch auf Platt
Ermittlungen laufen weiter: Leichenfund - 19-Jähriger soll Vater und Oma getötet haben
Diebstahl: Eier, Nudeln und Kartoffeln gestohlen
Wiederinbetriebnahme läuft: Zwei von fünf Kraftwerksblöcken nach Sabotage wieder am Netz
Unfälle: Sportboot sinkt nach Kollision mit Passagierschiff
Aus dem Zweiten Weltkrieg: Blindgänger in Neu-Ulm soll am Donnerstag entschärft werden
Basketball: Schwere Verletzung: MBC wochenlang ohne Kapitän Reaves
Sachsen-Anhalt: So lief das Duell zwischen Siegmund und Schulze
zeit.description: Die Kandidaten von AfD und CDU haben ein weiteres Mal diskutiert, es ging um Bildung, Migration, die Briefwahl und die Zukunft Sachsen-Anhalts. Das Liveblog zum Nachlesen

zeit.title: Katherina Reiche: Aus der Reihe getanzt
zeit.description: Mit ihrer Kritik an der Steuerreform hat sich die Wirtschaftsministerin als Unruheherd in der Regierung etabliert. Doch ihre größte Herausforderung steht erst noch bevor.

zeit.title: Umspannwerk bei Bergheim: Ermittler finden Abschussvorrichtungen nach Störung an Umspannwerk
zeit.description: Nach dem Vorfall an einem Umspannwerk bei Köln stoßen Ermittler auf Abschussvorrichtungen. Zuvor sprach der NRW-Innenminister von einem Verdacht auf Sabotage.

zeit.title: Marcant: Wie macht er das?
zeit.description: Dem YouTuber Marcant gelingt in Sachsen-Anhalt, was vielen Medien missglückt: ein offener Austausch mit AfD-Anhängern und Extremisten. Wie macht er das?

zeit.title: Moskau: Russland bestellt deutschen Geschäftsträger ein
zeit.description: Mit harten Worten reagieren die russischen Behörden auf die neuen Sanktionen der Bundesregierung. Das Außenministerium in Moskau spricht von »antirussischen Maßnahmen«.

zeit.title: Klimaziel der UN: 1,5-Grad-Ziel war gestern. Jetzt gilt der Overshoot
zeit.description: Das globale Klimaziel ist nicht zu halten. Wussten Sie schon? Aber jetzt sagen es auch die UN. Und skizzieren das Verfehlen gleich als vorübergehend. Wollen wir’s hoffen!

spiegel.title: Notenbank der Niederlande verlagert Gold von Nordamerika nach Großbritannien
spiegel.description: Die niederländische Notenbank hat 86 Tonnen Goldreserven von New York und Ottawa nach London verlagert. Die Bundesbank sieht noch keinen Handlungsbedarf.

spiegel.title: Annalena Baerbock: Ex-Außenministerin wehrt sich gegen Spott über Professur
spiegel.description: Annalena Baerbock wechselt von der Uno an die Universität und erntet dafür Kritik. Die frühere Außenministerin hat dafür vor allem eine Erklärung.

spiegel.title: Venezuela und die USA: »Trump sieht das Öl als Kriegsbeute«
spiegel.description: Mit einem Deal will der US-Präsident den Großteil des venezolanischen Öls übernehmen. Für das Land verheißt das nichts Gutes, sagt Experte Gustavo Coronel. Hier erläutert er die Folgen.

spiegel.title: Commerzbank-Chefin Bettina Orlopp bestätigt Gespräche mit UniCredit
spiegel.description: Lange wehrte sich die Commerzbank gegen eine Übernahme durch UniCredit. Jetzt berichtet Bankchefin Bettina Orlopp von direkten Gesprächen mit den Italienern – und warnt vor einer übereilten Integration.

spiegel.title: Aarau: Polizei bezeichnet Angriff bei Rave in der Schweiz als Amoklauf
spiegel.description: Bei dem tödlichen Angriff bei einem Rave im Schweizer Kanton Aargau hat es sich nach Polizeiangaben um einen Amoklauf gehandelt. Die Ermittler gehen von einem Einzeltäter aus.

spiegel.title: Bergheim in NRW: Ermittler finden sechs Abschussvorrichtungen auf Feld
spiegel.description: NRW-Innenminister Reul spricht von einem »Angriff auf unser Land«: Nach der Störung an einem Umspannwerk in Bergheim bei Köln haben die Ermittler sechs Abschussvorrichtungen in einem Feld gefunden.

spiegel.title: Marcant über seinen Kampf gegen die AfD: »Es gibt viele, die mich tot sehen wollen«
spiegel.description: Er geht auf Veranstaltungen der AfD, diskutiert mit Wählern – und wird massiv bedroht. Hier erzählt der YouTuber Marcant, warum er trotzdem weitermacht und den Osten warmherziger findet als den Westen.

spiegel.title: Forschung: Millionen Jahre altes Fossil entpuppt sich als Übergangsform
spiegel.description: Wie gingen Insekten an Land? Bislang stellte diese Frage ein Rätsel dar. Ein internationales Forschungsteam hat nun ein Fossil untersucht, das wohl ein Mischwesen war – und eine Lücke im Stammbaum schließt.

spiegel.title: Bergheim in NRW: Herbert Reul spricht von Anfangsverdacht der »verfassungsfeindlichen Sabotage« an Umspannwerk
spiegel.description: Nach dem Kurzschluss an einem Umspannwerk in Bergheim bei Köln gehen die Ermittler von einer Straftat aus. »Das war Absicht«, sagte NRW-Innenminister Herbert Reul. »Wer da ran geht, greift unser Land an«.

spiegel.title: Joseph Heß: Extremschwimmer durchschwimmt die Donau von der Quelle bis zur Mündung
spiegel.description: In 60 Tagen von Donaueschingen bis ans Schwarze Meer: Der Deutsche Joseph Heß hat die Donau in ihrer Gesamtlänge durchschwommen – und stieß auch auf die Folgen des Klimawandels.

spiegel.title: Jänschwalde: Terrorermittlungen nach Sabotage an Umspannwerk in Brandenburg
spiegel.description: Nach dem Angriff auf ein Umspannwerk am Kohlekraftwerk Jänschwalde im Süden Brandenburgs ermittelt die Polizei unter anderem wegen Terrorverdachts. Nach Tatverdächtigen werde weiter gesucht.

spiegel.title: Sekundäres Trauma: Diese Psychologin half traumatisierten Menschen. Und brauchte dann selbst Hilfe
spiegel.description: Pia Andreatta betreut seit Jahren Menschen in Notlagen. Besonders nach einem Einsatz ging es ihr selbst schlecht. Warum ein Trauma ansteckend sein kann und was ihr geholfen hat.

spiegel.title: AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt: Welche Löcher die Partei in den Haushalt reißen würde
spiegel.description: Ulrich Siegmund macht den Menschen in Sachsen-Anhalt vor der Wahl große Versprechungen. Die interaktive Grafik zeigt, was die AfD-Pläne kosten würden – und wie viele man kassieren müsste, um die Löcher im Haushalt zu stopfen.

spiegel.title: Unterfranken: ICE-Tür öffnet sich während Fahrt – Bundespolizei ermittelt
spiegel.description: Ein Schnellzug der Deutschen Bahn musste einen Nothalt einlegen. Eine Waggontür hatte sich während der Fahrt geöffnet. Die Polizei geht nach bisherigen Ermittlungen davon aus, dass jemand den Notfallknopf gedrückt hat.

spiegel.title: Kabinettsbeschluss zur Einkommensteuer: So berechnen Sie die Entlastung für Ihr Gehalt
spiegel.description: Trotz Kritik von Verbänden und Wirtschaftsministerin Reiche: Die Regierung hat die Pläne für eine Einkommensteuerreform abgesegnet. Unser Rechner zeigt, was das für Sie bedeutet.

spiegel.title: Energiewende: EU-Kommission genehmigt Reiche-Pläne für neue Gaskraftwerke
spiegel.description: In Deutschland sollen nach Plänen von Wirtschaftsministerin Reiche zahlreiche neue Gaskraftwerke entstehen. Die EU-Kommission hat die Investitionen in Milliardenhöhe nun genehmigt. Eine Frage ist aber noch offen.

spiegel.title: Wetter in Deutschland: Hitze-Comeback mit mehr als 30 Grad im Süden

phys-org.title: A 13-meter rocket hit the Moon: Tasmanian researchers helped track it there

In the days before impact, University of Tasmania researchers from the School of Natural Sciences were the first in the world to detect the object by radar, helping refine predictions of where it would land.

phys-org.title: Physicists test the weak equivalence principle in an orbiting space station
phys-org.description: The weak equivalence principle (WEP) is central to Einstein's general relativity. It posits that gravity must accelerate everything equally, regardless of what it is made from. For the first time, a team led by Ming-Sheng Zhan at the Wuhan Institute of Physics and Mathematics has tested the principle using clouds of continuously free-falling atoms aboard an orbiting space station.

phys-org.title: A summer odyssey: Female dotterels seek multiple mates across Northern Europe
phys-org.description: On a high Norwegian plateau in late May, patches of bare ground begin to appear through the snow, and with them arrive some of Europe's most approachable birds. Eurasian dotterels breed on exposed mountain ridges and Arctic tundra from Scotland, through Scandinavia, to Siberia, and are famously tolerant of people—a trait that has long made them easy prey for hunters. They are unusual in another sense, too.

phys-org.title: Floridians become more cautious as economic outlook weakens in August

phys-org.title: Despite years of rain, Blue Mountains forests still haven't recovered from the Black Summer megafires
phys-org.description: For three years before the Black Summer megafires of 2019–20, cool-season rainfall in southeastern Australia was only half the normal amount. When fires broke out, intensely dry conditions helped them spread through areas typically resistant to burning, such as wetlands and rainforests.

phys-org.title: Beneficial bacteria support tomato growth and suppress disease
phys-org.description: Bacterial canker, a vascular infection, can wreak havoc on tomato plants, with symptoms ranging from wilted leaves to the collapse of an entire plant. Clavibacter michiganensis, the seedborne pathogen that causes the disease, can be challenging to treat because it spreads easily. "This pathogen is really problematic, especially in greenhouses," said microbiologist Eric Déziel, Ph.D., at the Institut national de la recherche scientifique (INRS) in Quebec, Canada.

phys-org.title: Seven new species show 250-million-year-old marine group is still evolving

phys-org.title: New research: Google's AI Overviews reinforce some conspiracy theories

phys-org.description: Astronomers have discovered a second interstellar cloud near the center of the Milky Way that is extraordinarily rich in complex molecules, including several molecules associated with prebiotic chemistry. The newly studied cloud, G+0.633-0.0604, or G+0.633, contains more than 120 identified molecular species and is the first confirmed chemical twin of another famous molecule-rich cloud. Their paper, posted to the arXiv preprint server on Aug. 14, outlines the chemistry of the newfound cloud.

phys-org.title: UN report finds 1.5°C warming limit likely to be exceeded by 2030

phys-org.title: Are remote workers more or less productive?

phys-org.title: Q&A: Can U.S. parks promote safety, recreation and environmental protection?

In U.S. national parks, maintaining visitor safety can be complicated because it is difficult to measure who is in a park and where they are, much less what hazards they will face as extreme weather events become more common, according to Bing Pan, professor of recreation, park and tourism management at Penn State.

These ornaments can include colorful plumage, elaborate tails or fins, inflatable throat sacs and elongated eye stalks.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?

But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

proj-syn.title: AI’s Market Path Will Get Bumpier
proj-syn.description: By enhancing the input that goes into so much of what we do—intelligence—AI’s potential to drive higher economic growth is enormous. But with fears of the technology's unintended consequences affecting the pace and depth of adoption, the promise of long-term gains must be set against more immediate risks.

proj-syn.title: American Götterdämmerung
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump and his Treasury secretary’s latest desperate threats confirm how much American power has waned on their watch. Far from compelling others to join their efforts to isolate Iran, they are hastening the transition to a post-American world order.

proj-syn.title: Hard Lessons for Europe From the Ceuta Crisis
proj-syn.description: European Union leaders should have received several messages during the recent surge of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta. In particular, cohesion without trust is fragile; dependence without limits leads to vulnerability; and selective enforcement of international law risks eroding a pillar of Europe’s strategic identity.

proj-syn.title: The World’s Silent Majority for International Cooperation
proj-syn.description: The hollowing out of global institutions has resulted in a rapid loss of credibility for the international rule of law. But a majority of people worldwide still recognize the value of multilateralism, which countries can preserve in the absence of superpower consent by finding better ways to cooperate.

proj-syn.title: Building Canada’s Post-American Economy
proj-syn.description: Canada’s dependence on the US market has become a strategic liability, leaving it vulnerable to President Donald Trump’s bullying. Reducing that dependence will require building industries that can compete globally while removing the structural barriers that prevent innovative Canadian firms from scaling.

proj-syn.title: Trump and Xi Should Align on AI
proj-syn.description: When potential outcomes are systemic and irreversible, preparation must precede certainty. This is the logic behind insurance, as well as every pandemic plan and arms-control treaty ever created, and it must be the principle that guides our approach to AI—beginning at the upcoming US-China summit.

proj-syn.title: The Quiet Revolution in Services
proj-syn.description: While economists debate whether industrialization can still play its traditional growth-promoting role in the current global and technological context, services have unexpectedly become an engine for economic development around the world. For developing and developed economies alike, the timing could not be better.

proj-syn.title: AI Addicts Won’t Make Better Workers
proj-syn.description: Economists widely agree that AI will boost labor productivity. But this view does not account for the possibility that hyperscalers will go all out to get people hooked on LLMs, because the narrower applications for which these tools are actually useful do not justify the massive investments made so far.

proj-syn.title: Latin America’s Crime Tax
proj-syn.description: Even excluding lives lost, communities displaced, and families ravaged, the economic costs of organized crime in the region produce a bleak picture, shaving 0.5–2 percentage points off annual GDP growth in the most affected countries. That, too, represents a hefty human toll.

proj-syn.title: Are The Walls Closing in on Bessent?
proj-syn.description: Far from suggesting financial Armageddon, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s futile efforts to keep a lid on Treasury yields suggest that, once again, the dollar is America’s currency, but everyone else’s problem. But while investors have few alternatives, the bond-salesman-in-chief cannot be complacent.

proj-syn.title: AI Is Reviving Chinese Marxist Economics
proj-syn.description: As recently as two years ago, most Chinese economists paid only lip service to Marxism and assigned Western textbooks to their students. The advent of AI has changed that, because the technology—open source and available to the smallest manufacturer for a pittance—promises to avoid the “rent trap” common to capitalist economies.

proj-syn.title: Gen Z Is Transforming South Asia
proj-syn.description: Facing diminished economic prospects, many young people see not flawed institutions in need of gradual reform, but predatory systems robbing them of their future. Across South Asia, this sense has animated powerful protest movements, some of which could shape their countries' political trajectories for decades to come.

proj-syn.title: How Britain Can Help Build a Fairer Global Economy
proj-syn.description: With the United Kingdom poised to preside over both the G20 and the G7, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has a unique opportunity to usher in a new internationalism grounded not in military posturing, but in the pursuit of a fairer global economy. But he must abandon his predecessor’s defensive approach.

proj-syn.title: Technocracy Can’t Fix Europe
proj-syn.description: A new private initiative bringing together the crème de la crème of European business, financial, economic, and tech elites could well prove useful in kick-starting European growth and innovation. But first, it must recognize that the problem it hopes to solve is fundamentally political.

proj-syn.title: The Fed and the Treasury Are in Denial
proj-syn.description: For most of the postwar era, the United States has enjoyed a privileged position as an issuer of both sovereign debt and US dollars that always found takers. But the US may no longer be able to rely on stable demand for its debt or its currency, forcing policymakers to face the truth about how financial markets are made.

proj-syn.title: To End Global Hunger, Invest in Rural Communities
proj-syn.description: Even as hunger declines around the world, food insecurity remains prevalent in rural communities. Restoring soil health, expanding access to new technologies, strengthening land rights, and upgrading public infrastructure are essential to boost agricultural productivity and protect rural livelihoods.

proj-syn.title: The Sanctions Illusion
proj-syn.description: Those who defend sweeping financial sanctions against countries like Russia and Iran often claim that popular suffering is a defensible means of pressuring the target government. But while such measures certainly inflict widespread suffering on civilian populations, this rarely translates into political change.

proj-syn.title: Is Monetarism Making a Comeback?
proj-syn.description: After decades on the margins of mainstream economic thinking, monetarism is beginning to re-enter the debate, most notably at the Federal Reserve. To regain credibility, however, monetarists must learn from past mistakes and adapt to the monetary and financial realities of the 21st century.
